display_name: YASKAWA Motoman robot controller (High-Speed Ethernet Server, FS100 protocol)

mapping_provenance.0x70.alarm_code: HW1481031 s3.3.1 (p.3-20), command 0x70 attribute 1 'Alarm code'. Vendor-stated range 0x0001 to 0x270F (decimal 9999). Instance 1-4 selects which of the four pendant-displayed alarms; this row is instance 1, the LATEST alarm. POLARITY (higher is worse) IS PACK-AUTHOR JUDGEMENT - the manual states no polarity. The code is NOT ordinal: a higher number is a different alarm, not a worse one, so the polarity flag here means 'non-zero is bad', not 'monotone'.
mapping_provenance.0x70.alarm_name: HW1481031 s3.3.1 (p.3-22), command 0x70 attribute 5 'Alarm character strings name', elements 8-15, 32 letters. Manual NOTE: 'Use the same language code as the FS100, or the characters corrupt'. The sub code (attribute 2 'Alarm data') is NOT mapped - the manual's 28-value 'Alarm type' enum says how to RENDER it ([SLURBT], [XYZ], bit patterns, ...) and no canonical field can hold a type-tagged sub code.
mapping_provenance.0x72.data1.bit3_running: HW1481031 s3.3.3 (p.3-26), command 0x72 instance 1 attribute 1, Data 1 bit3 'Running'. A BOOLEAN mapped onto a string enum field: 1 must decode to `running` and 0 to `idle`. The manual gives no text token, so the pack declares the wire tokens as '0'/'1' and relies on the registry decoder.
mapping_provenance.0x72.data1.bit5_teach: HW1481031 s3.3.3 (p.3-26) Data 1 bit5 'Teach'. Data 1 bits 5 and 6 (Teach/Play) are a ONE-HOT MODE PAIR encoded as separate booleans, not a scalar. Both rows target robot.operating_mode, so a consumer that receives both will see whichever arrives last. That is a real defect of this mapping and is recorded rather than hidden: the HSES wire format has no single mode word to map.
mapping_provenance.0x72.data1.bit6_play: HW1481031 s3.3.3 (p.3-26) Data 1 bit6 'Play'. See the one-hot warning on 0x72.data1.bit5_teach.
mapping_provenance.0x72.data2.bit1_hold_pendant: HW1481031 s3.3.3 (p.3-26), Data 2 bit1 'In hold status (by programming pendant)'. Three DISTINCT hold causes (bits 1, 2, 3) all collapse onto robot.program.state, which loses the cause. The cause is the operationally useful part (an externally-held robot is a line problem; a pendant-held robot is a person) and no canonical field preserves it.
mapping_provenance.0x72.data2.bit2_hold_external: HW1481031 s3.3.3 (p.3-26), Data 2 bit2 'In hold status (externally)'. See the cause-collapse note on bit1.
mapping_provenance.0x72.data2.bit3_hold_command: HW1481031 s3.3.3 (p.3-26), Data 2 bit3 'In hold status (by command)'. See the cause-collapse note on bit1.
mapping_provenance.0x72.data2.bit4_alarming: HW1481031 s3.3.3 (p.3-26), Data 2 bit4 'Alarming'. MAPPED ONTO emergency_stop_active, WHICH IS NOT WHAT IT MEANS: 'Alarming' is an alarm condition, an E-stop is a specific safety circuit, and the manual's status words contain no E-stop bit at all. There is no canonical field for a generic controller alarm boolean. This row is the clearest case in this pack of a documented value with no canonical home, and it should be reviewed before anyone trusts emergency_stop_active from a Motoman.
mapping_provenance.0x72.data2.bit6_servo_on: HW1481031 s3.3.3 (p.3-26), Data 2 bit6 'Servo ON'. POLARITY (higher is better) IS PACK-AUTHOR JUDGEMENT. Data 2 bit0 and bit7 are left BLANK in the manual's own table and are deliberately not mapped.
mapping_provenance.0x73.job_name: HW1481031 s3.3.4 (p.3-27), command 0x73 attribute 1 'Job name (character strings: 32 letters)', 'Half-width character: 32 characters / Full-width character: 16 characters'. Instance 1 = Master task; instances 2-6 are sub tasks 1-5 and are NOT mapped (no canonical field distinguishes concurrent tasks).
mapping_provenance.0x73.speed_override: HW1481031 s3.3.4 (p.3-28), attribute 4 'Speed override value'. THE MANUAL STATES NO UNIT AND NO RANGE FOR THIS ITEM. `%` is declared here by pack-author judgement because s3.3.39 uses 0.01% for a commanded LINK speed, but that is a DIFFERENT command and the inference is explicitly unverified. If the wire value is really 0.01%, every reading from this row is 100x too large. RETARGETED after a live resolve: the first draft mapped this onto robot.speed_scaling, whose registry physics_bounds are [0, 1] (a RATIO, not a percent) and unit is null - so 100 was rejected at read time as 'physics_violation: 100 outside [0, 1]' and the reading was nulled. sensor_readings.speed_override declares unit '%' and bounds [0, 100]. The compiler's dimension check could not catch the original because a field with unit null has no dimension to compare against; see the scale check added for that class.
mapping_provenance.0x73.step_no: HW1481031 s3.3.4 (p.3-28), attribute 3 'Step No. (1 to 9998)'. Mapped to sequence_number rather than a line number: a step is a motion instruction index, not a text line.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i1.axis1_s: HW1481031 s3.3.6 (p.3-31), command 0x75 INSTANCE 1 = 'R1 ... Robot (pulse value)', attribute 6. THE WIRE VALUE IS ENCODER PULSES, NOT DEGREES. `deg` is declared in tag_units so the value lands in a field with an angle dimension, and that declaration is WRONG on the wire: pulses-per-degree is a per-model, per-axis constant the manual does not publish and this pack cannot supply. This row is included because the S/L/U/R/B/T axis ORDER is vendor-documented (s3.3.5 Axis Configuration Information) and the axis identity is the useful part; the magnitude must not be trusted until a pulses-per-degree table is sourced.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i1.axis2_l: HW1481031 s3.3.6, instance 1 attribute 7. See the PULSES-NOT-DEGREES warning on axis1_s.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i1.axis3_u: HW1481031 s3.3.6, instance 1 attribute 8. See the PULSES-NOT-DEGREES warning on axis1_s.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i1.axis4_r: HW1481031 s3.3.6, instance 1 attribute 9. See the PULSES-NOT-DEGREES warning on axis1_s.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i1.axis5_b: HW1481031 s3.3.6, instance 1 attribute 10. See the PULSES-NOT-DEGREES warning on axis1_s.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i1.axis6_t: HW1481031 s3.3.6, instance 1 attribute 11. See the PULSES-NOT-DEGREES warning on axis1_s.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i101.axis1_x: HW1481031 s3.3.6 (p.3-31), command 0x75 INSTANCE 101 = 'R1 ... Robot (cartesian coordinate)', attribute 6 'First axis data'. Unit um per s3.3.39 (p.3-81) 'X coordinate value ... unit: um'. TWO VENDOR-STATED TRAPS: (a) elements 6-13 are PULSES when instance is 1-23 and Cartesian when instance is 101-102, so element 1 'Data type' (0 = Pulse value, 16 = Base coordinate value) MUST be read before interpreting; (b) the manual states '0 is set to nonexistent axis' - 0 means the axis is ABSENT, not at the origin. Neither can be expressed in this pack schema.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i101.axis2_y: HW1481031 s3.3.6 / s3.3.39 'Y coordinate value ... unit: um'. See the Data-type and zero-means-absent traps on axis1_x.
mapping_provenance.0x75.i101.axis3_z: HW1481031 s3.3.6 / s3.3.39 'Z coordinate value ... unit: um'. See the traps on axis1_x. The manual also notes the read path can select the BASE coordinate only: 'Cartesian value can select the base coordinate only. (It cannot select the robot, user and tool coordinates.)' - so these are base-frame, not tool-frame, positions.
mapping_provenance.0x77.axis1: HW1481031 s3.3.8 (p.3-35), command 0x77: 'Torque data of each axis can be read out.' THE MANUAL STATES NO UNIT, NO RANGE AND NO SIGN CONVENTION. No tag_units entry is declared, deliberately: a guessed unit here would be converted at confidence 1.0. Commonly reported elsewhere as percent of rated torque; that was NOT verified against any vendor document. POLARITY (higher is worse) IS PACK-AUTHOR JUDGEMENT and applies to the MAGNITUDE - the sign convention is unknown.
mapping_provenance.0x77.axis2: HW1481031 s3.3.8 (p.3-35), attribute 2. Unit undocumented - see axis1.
mapping_provenance.0x77.axis3: HW1481031 s3.3.8 (p.3-35), attribute 3. Unit undocumented - see axis1.
mapping_provenance.0x77.axis4: HW1481031 s3.3.8 (p.3-35), attribute 4. Unit undocumented - see axis1.
mapping_provenance.0x77.axis5: HW1481031 s3.3.8 (p.3-35), attribute 5. Unit undocumented - see axis1.
mapping_provenance.0x77.axis6: HW1481031 s3.3.8 (p.3-35), attribute 6. Unit undocumented - see axis1.
mapping_provenance.0x88.i1.elapse_time: HW1481031 s3.3.25 (p.3-57), command 0x88 instance 1 'Control power ON time', attribute 2 'Elapse time'. THE VALUE IS A CHARACTER STRING, NOT A NUMBER: 'Character strings: 12 characters - Ex. 000000:00'00', i.e. HHHHHH:MM'SS with a six-digit hour field. Declaring `h` presumes a parse this pack cannot perform - nothing in the engine parses HHHHHH:MM'SS, so this row will arrive as an unparseable string unless the collector converts it first.
mapping_provenance.0x88.i10.elapse_time: HW1481031 s3.3.25 (p.3-57), instance 10 'Servo power ON time (TOTAL)'. Same HHHHHH:MM'SS string-format problem as instance 1. Per-group instances 11-12 (R1-R2) and 21-23 (S1-S3) exist and are not mapped - no canonical field is per-control-group.
mapping_provenance.0x88.i210.elapse_time: HW1481031 s3.3.25 (p.3-57), instance 210 'Motion time (TOTAL)'. Same string-format problem.
mapping_provenance.0x88.i301.elapse_time: HW1481031 s3.3.25 (p.3-57), instance 301 of '301 to 308: Operation time'. The manual does NOT say what distinguishes operation times 301..308, so only 301 is mapped and the other seven are left unmapped rather than guessed. Same string-format problem. `s` is declared because cycle_time_seconds is the only cycle-shaped canonical field, which is a poor fit for a cumulative counter.
mapping_provenance.0x89.i11.model_name: HW1481031 s3.3.26 (p.3-58), command 0x89 instance 11 'Type information (R1)', attribute 2 'Model name / application', 16 characters, 'Ex. (For model) MPP0003-A0*'. The manual notes a NULL string is returned for instances 21-23 (stations).

not_mapped.0x30A / 0x30B / 0x8A / 0x8B: Table 3-1 footnote: 'available for system software version FS1.14 or higher'. That is an FS100 version string and its applicability to YRC1000 is unverified.
not_mapped.0x70 attribute 2 'Alarm data' (sub code): The 28-value 'Alarm type' enum (s3.3.1) decides how the sub code renders - decimal, bit pattern, [SLURBT] axis list, [XYZ] coordinate, control-group list. No canonical field can hold a type-tagged value.
not_mapped.0x70 attribute 4 'Alarm occurring time': 16-character string 'Ex. 2011/10/10 15:49'. No canonical field for an alarm timestamp distinct from the reading timestamp.
not_mapped.0x71 Alarm history: s3.3.2 (p.3-23). The instance ranges ARE the alarm category enumeration (1-100 Major failure, 1001-1100 Monitor alarm, 2001-2100 User alarm system, 3001-3100 User alarm user, 4001-4100 OFF line alarm). History is a list, not a reading; the normalizer takes one value per tag per observation.
not_mapped.0x75 'Form' and 'Extended form' bit word: s3.3.6 (p.3-32). Fully enumerated by the vendor (bit0 Front/Back, bit1 Upper/Lower arm, bit2 Flip/No flip, bit3-5 theta R/T/S >=180, bit6 Redundant front/back, bit7 reverse-conversion source; Extended form bit0-4 theta L/U/B/E/W >=180). No canonical field holds a robot configuration word.
not_mapped.0x75 'Tool number' / 'User coordinate nu: s3.3.6 attributes 3 and 4, ranges 0-63 and 1-63 (s3.3.39). They change what the position MEANS; no canonical field represents the active frame.
not_mapped.0x76 Position Error Reading: HW1481031 s3.3.7 (p.3-34). The manual states no unit, no range and no sign convention. Following error is one of the most useful robot health signals and it is omitted BECAUSE the unit is undocumented - mapping it would store an unknown quantity into a bounded field at confidence 1.0.
not_mapped.0x78 / 0x79 I/O and register data: Table 3-1 names the commands; which I/O number means what is in the FS100 Concurrent I/O manual, which was not obtained.
not_mapped.0x84 CYCLE (STEP / 1 CYCLE / CONTINUE): HW1481031 s3.3.21 (p.3-55), data element 1 = '1: STEP / 2: 1 CYCLE / 3: CONTINUE'. WITHDRAWN BY THE COMPILER'S missing_decoder REFUSAL. The only mode-shaped canonical fields (machine_mode, execution_state) carry canonical_values ['running','idle','stopped','error','unknown'] - a run state, not a job-advance mode - so all three vendor values would have had to collapse onto 'running' and the distinction a step-mode robot exists to express would be lost. Needs a new canonical field, which is a registry change, not a pack change. Original citation: HW1481031 s3.3.21 (p.3-55), command 0x84 instance 2 'CYCLE (switching of STEP/CYCLE/CONTINUE)', data element 1 = '1: STEP / 2: 1 CYCLE / 3: CONTINUE'. This is the SCALAR counterpart to Data 1 bits 0-2 in s3.3.3 and is the better mode source for that reason. It is documented as a WRITE command whose current value is readable with Get_Attribute_Single (0x0E) per the s3.2 service model.
not_mapped.MotoPlus API: No MotoPlus SDK documentation was read. Nothing in this pack comes from MotoPlus.
not_mapped.ROS-Industrial Simple Message: github.com/ros-industrial/motoman motoman_motion_reply.h enumerates a useful not-ready taxonomy (ALARM, ERROR, ESTOP, NOT_PLAY, NOT_REMOTE, SERVO_OFF, HOLD, PFL_ACTIVE, ...) that maps one-for-one onto the HSES status bits. It is a DIFFERENT interface on a different port and no document asserts the correspondence, so it is not used as a source here.

source: YASKAWA/Motoman 'FS100 OPTIONS INSTRUCTIONS FOR HIGH-SPEED ETHERNET SERVER FUNCTION', MANUAL NO. HW1481031 (part 160766-1CD), sections 3.2 (packet layout, UDP 10040/10041), Table 3-1 List of Robot Control Command (pp.3-17..3-19), 3.3.1 Alarm Data Reading (pp.3-20..3-22), 3.3.3 Status Information Reading (p.3-26), 3.3.4 Executing Job Information Reading (pp.3-27..3-28), 3.3.6 Robot Position Data Reading (pp.3-31..3-33), 3.3.7 Position Error Reading (p.3-34), 3.3.8 Torque Data Reading (p.3-35), 3.3.25 Management Time Acquiring (p.3-57), 3.3.26 System Information Acquiring (p.3-58), 3.3.39 Move Instruction Cartesian (pp.3-81..3-82). Fetched from motoman.com 2026-10-03.
vendor_native_note: SCOPE WARNING, READ BEFORE DEPLOYING. Every fact in this pack is from the FS100 manual HW1481031. No YRC1000, YRC1000micro or DX200 HSES manual was obtained, so the aliases yrc1000/yrc1000micro rest on third-party evidence only: github.com/masayuki-kono/moto-hses reports YRC1000micro VERIFIED against this same FS100-documented protocol and YRC1000/DX200/FS100 'not verified'. Tag spellings are `<cmd>.<attribute>` using the manual's own command numbers and attribute names, because the HSES wire format is numeric (command/instance/attribute) and has no tag names of its own - the spelling is this pack's convention, the numbers are the vendor's.
